# data-navigator Tech Radar

Shared dependency guidance for an **offline-first Electron + Next.js 16 desktop data-analysis app** targeting a **medium-end PC with no guaranteed WebGPU and no runtime internet**. Synthesized from 9 research briefs. Per-feature planners: read the domain that applies, then check the Adopt/Trial/Hold list at the end.

## Cross-cutting principles (read first)

- **The existing stack is already ~90% correct.** Default move is **consolidation + graceful-fallback hardening**, not wholesale replacement. Most "new" items below are dev-only tools or narrowly-scoped specialists.
- **WebGPU is opportunistic, never required.** ~70-82% global coverage but frequently disabled on Linux, integrated/older GPUs, and enterprise policy. **WASM-SIMD + INT8 CPU is the guaranteed baseline**; WebGPU is an auto-detected upgrade with mandatory CPU fallback. This single rule rejects `@mlc-ai/web-llm` as any primary path.
- **Two-process discipline.** Heavy native work (DuckDB, llama.cpp, ONNX node, large export streaming) runs in **Electron main/utility process**. Heavy browser work (DuckDB-WASM, ONNX-web, embeddings, OPFS SyncAccessHandle, rasterization) runs in **Web Workers via Comlink** — never the renderer main thread.
- **Storage split:** OPFS `createSyncAccessHandle` (Worker-only) for large blobs (Parquet, model weights) ~10x faster than IndexedDB; Dexie/IndexedDB for many small structured records. Always call `navigator.storage.persist()` at startup and surface `estimate()` quota.
- **Local-first SYNC engines (ElectricSQL/Zero/PowerSync/Convex) violate the offline-only constraint** — they require a server + Postgres. The offline-safe primitives are **CRDTs (Yjs/Loro/Automerge)** and TinyBase, optionally over a LAN-only hub.
- **Cross-origin isolation (COOP: same-origin + COEP: require-corp)** unlocks SharedArrayBuffer → WASM threads + DuckDB-WASM COI bundle. Electron can set these unconditionally on its custom protocol — a real advantage over the browser path.
- All recommendations run with **zero network at runtime**; model/WASM assets are bundled or cached-once in OPFS/IndexedDB. Licenses are permissive (MIT/ISC/Apache-2.0/BSD) except axe-core (MPL-2.0, tool use only).

## Domain 2 — Analytical data engine (DuckDB, Arrow, Parquet)

**Primary engine is the native DuckDB main-process path — do NOT migrate the desktop to DuckDB-WASM.** Native is 5-50x faster, no SharedArrayBuffer/COOP-COEP constraint, no 4GB WASM ceiling, real OS threads/SIMD. The existing "CSV → managed Parquet cache → exposed as views" design is exactly right (pays CSV parse cost once, every later query is fast + seekable). Push compute to SQL (LIMIT/aggregate/window), stream results as Arrow, virtualize the UI — never materialize big results on the main thread.

## Domain 3 — Local LLM + embeddings (on-device inference)

**Two-lane architecture.** Lane A: `node-llama-cpp` in the Electron main/utility process is the **PRIMARY generative LLM engine** (GGUF q4, auto GPU offload + CPU AVX, in-process, no daemon). Lane B: `@huggingface/transformers` in a Web Worker is the **PRIMARY embedding engine** + browser-only LLM fallback. Structured JSON (chart specs, SQL, filters) is a **solved problem on the llama.cpp side via GBNF / JSON-schema grammars** enforced at token sampling — a decisive edge over browser engines. Token generation is memory-bandwidth-bound: quantization + small models matter more than cores.

**Model defaults:** Embeddings → `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim, ~23MB int8, <30ms CPU); upgrade option `bge-small-en-v1.5`/`gte-small`. Generative → `Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B-Instruct` q4_K_M (best structured-output behavior at size); low-RAM fallback `Qwen2.5-0.5B` / `SmolLM2-1.7B`. Avoid >3B on 8GB RAM.

## Domain 4 — Data visualization & large-grid rendering

**Canvas 2D + WASM-SIMD first, WebGL2 second, WebGPU opportunistic.** ~45% of older/iGPU devices fall to compat mode. The project already ships ECharts 6, Recharts 3, Vega/Vega-Lite 6, TanStack Table/Virtual, react-force-graph. **Rationalize by role, don't add more** — except uPlot for dense time-series and (Trial) Perspective for interactive pivots. **OffscreenCanvas + Worker rendering (via Comlink) is the single biggest 60fps lever** on medium CPUs; ECharts and Chart.js support it.

**Grid by row count:** TanStack Table + Virtual (DOM) up to ~50-100k rows with full React cell control → canvas grid (glide-data-grid / Perspective) for 100k-millions or heavy streaming.
**Marks by count:** SVG/Vega-Lite ≤~1-10k → Canvas (ECharts/uPlot) >~1k → WebGL/deck.gl >~100k-1M+ or geospatial.
**Charts-to-image:** use native `echarts.getDataURL()`/`renderToSVGString()` and serialize recharts `<svg>` directly — never DOM-screenshot charts.

## Domain 5 — Offline geospatial mapping

**Token-free, zero-network stack:** MapLibre GL JS (renderer) + Protomaps PMTiles basemap + self-hosted glyphs/sprites + deck.gl `MapboxOverlay({interleaved:true})` for points + `@geoarrow/deck.gl-layers` fed zero-copy from DuckDB Arrow + supercluster-in-worker for clustering + h3-js for hexbin analytics + tippecanoe (build-time) for user-data tiling. WebGL2 baseline matches the no-WebGPU constraint. **You MUST self-host glyphs (fonts .pbf) and sprites locally** — MapLibre fetches them at runtime from the style.

**iGPU point budgets:** ~100k-500k smooth; aggregate beyond. For 1M+ points never pass plain JS arrays — use binary/GeoArrow buffers (biggest perf+memory win). supercluster = zoom-reactive clustering UX; h3-js = fixed-resolution analytical hexbins (complementary, not competitors). Tile generation is an offline **build step**, not runtime.

## Domain 6 — Statistics, forecasting & ML

**Tiered forecasting** (avoids heavy deps on the hot path): (1) hand-roll Holt-Winters / EWMA / simple exponential smoothing (~150 lines TS in a worker, deterministic, tiny); (2) vendored `arima` WASM for ARIMA/SARIMA when needed; (3) Pyodide+statsmodels/Prophet as **opt-in "advanced" mode only** (cache once in OPFS). **Anomaly/change-point detection is a genuine library gap** — implement S-H-ESD, MAD, EWMA, CUSUM, PELT in-house (small, well-specified) atop an STL decomposition; budget engineering, not a dependency.

## Domain 7 — Document export & reporting

**Run ALL heavy export work in Electron main/Node or a Worker — never the renderer main thread** (jsPDF-autotable OOMs/hangs past a few k rows). Stream/paginate, write to disk incrementally via `fs`, free buffers between chunks.

**PDF = split stack:** `pdfmake` for data-driven tabular reports (auto-paginates large tables); `@cantoo/pdf-lib` fork for merge/stamp/fill (original pdf-lib is stale); keep `jspdf`+autotable for simple/quick only. Avoid `@react-pdf/renderer` for very large tables.
**XLSX:** `exceljs` streaming `WorkbookWriter` (~6x less memory than SheetJS, which is in-memory only and off public npm). **Swap `html2canvas` (stale) → `html-to-image`** for DOM-to-image. **Never screenshot charts** — use native ECharts `getDataURL()` / recharts `<svg>` serialization.

## Domain 8 — Local-first collaboration (no cloud)

**Yjs is the default** — MIT, ~18kB pure-JS (no WASM), low memory, mature ecosystem, already a dependency; runs fully in-process with no cloud. Presence is native via `y-protocols` Awareness (prefer raw Awareness + your own hook over unmaintained y-presence). **Reject ElectricSQL & PowerSync** — both are Postgres↔SQLite SYNC engines requiring a server; CRDTs are the correct cloudless primitive.

**Offline persistence:** y-indexeddb (renderer) or custom Electron-main file/SQLite persistence, gated on `whenStored`. **P2P over LAN, two ways:** (A) `y-webrtc` + a locally-bundled signaling server (disable public STUN/signaling); (B) Hocuspocus embedded in Electron main as a localhost/LAN hub — the **more reliable offline default** (WebRTC mDNS/NAT often blocked on locked-down LANs). Discover the hub via mDNS (`bonjour-service`) with a UDP-broadcast fallback.

**CRDT perf:** Loro fastest/smallest > Yjs strong second > Automerge slowest/heaviest. For medium-end + existing Yjs investment, Yjs's no-WASM low-memory profile wins today; Loro is the trending spike candidate if doc history/branching is needed.

## Domain 10 — Dev tooling & quality (offline, dev-only)

Repo is already on best-in-class hygiene (knip 6, dependency-cruiser 17, sherif, publint, size-limit 12, @next/bundle-analyzer). **Enable rather than add:** knip strict/CI gating + plugin coverage (Vitest/Storybook/Playwright/Next); depcruise circular + forbidden-dependency rules; size-limit `@size-limit/preset-app` + time plugin with **per-route/per-worker budgets** (heavy workers: onnxruntime-web, transformers.js, web-llm, vad, sherpa). Lighthouse/axe/Vitest-bench all run **fully offline against localhost / bundled Chromium**. Net-new deps are small dev-only: Sonda, react-scan, @lhci/cli (+ optional unlighthouse/madge/wasm-opt).

## Adopt / Trial / Hold

### ADOPT — proven, keep or wire in now
- **Architecture/persistence:** comlink, dexie, OPFS, @electron/fuses, COOP/COEP headers, serwist (pinned)
- **Data engine:** @duckdb/node-api (native, primary), apache-arrow, arquero
- **LLM/ML:** node-llama-cpp (Electron primary), @huggingface/transformers (browser embeddings primary), onnxruntime-web, onnxruntime-node, sherpa-onnx; GBNF/JSON-schema grammars for structured output; all-MiniLM-L6-v2 + Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B defaults
- **Viz/grid:** ECharts 6, TanStack Table/Virtual, Vega/Vega-Lite; uPlot (dense time-series); OffscreenCanvas+Worker rendering; native chart→image export
- **Geospatial:** maplibre-gl, pmtiles, @protomaps/basemaps (+ self-hosted glyphs/sprites), deck.gl, supercluster (in worker), h3-js, tippecanoe (build-time)
- **Stats:** simple-statistics, @stdlib/stats, ml-matrix, ml-kmeans, ml-dbscan; in-house Holt-Winters/EWMA/STL/MAD/S-H-ESD/CUSUM/PELT
- **Export:** pdfmake, exceljs (streaming), docx, pptxgenjs, html-to-image; @cantoo/pdf-lib (pinned); keep jspdf for light exports
- **Collab:** yjs, y-indexeddb, y-protocols Awareness, y-websocket, @hocuspocus/server (Electron-main hub), bonjour-service
- **Vector:** sqlite-vec
- **Dev tooling:** knip (strict/CI), dependency-cruiser, size-limit (per-route/worker), axe-core, tinybench, sonda, react-scan, @lhci/cli, binaryen wasm-opt, web-vitals

### TRIAL — spike behind a flag / scope carefully
- **@duckdb/duckdb-wasm** — only if a non-Electron web build ships (browser fallback engine)
- **@uwdata/flechette / hyparquet / parquet-wasm** — lighter renderer Arrow/Parquet paths
- **FINOS Perspective** — interactive pivot grid over millions of rows
- **glide-data-grid** — canvas grid beyond TanStack DOM limits (verify maintenance first)
- **deck.gl + @geoarrow/deck.gl-layers** — 1M+ point/geospatial layers from DuckDB Arrow
- **@lancedb/lancedb** — vector search when corpus outgrows sqlite-vec
- **loro-crdt** — if document history/branching becomes a requirement
- **tinybase** — lighter reactive store alternative to @tanstack/db
- **arima (vendored, frozen) / stlnode** — forecasting + STL, worker-isolated, with `.destroy()` discipline
- **Pyodide + statsmodels/Prophet** — opt-in advanced forecasting tier, cached once
- **wllama** — CPU-only in-renderer LLM fallback (needs COOP/COEP)
- **Ollama + electron-ollama** — documented power-user escape hatch
- **unlighthouse / madge** — multi-page audits / circular-dep docs
- **react-map-gl, docx-templates, density-clustering (OPTICS), web-vitals RUM** — narrow opt-ins
- **anofox-forecast (Rust/WASM)** — WATCH for stale-`arima` replacement once JS bindings mature

### HOLD — do not adopt as primary (or reject)
- **@mlc-ai/web-llm** — WebGPU-required, no CPU fallback; fails on medium/iGPU/Linux. High-end-GPU accelerator only, never primary
- **@tanstack/db** — beta + API/sync-oriented; not the offline source of truth yet (scoped trial only)
- **html2canvas** — stale/experimental; fallback for canvas/WebGL captures only
- **@react-pdf/renderer** — avoid for large tabular exports (memory/CPU heavy)
- **sheetjs (xlsx)** — in-memory only (OOM on big writes) + off public npm; format breadth only
- **jspdf-autotable** — light tables only; OOMs past a few k rows
- **jstat** — stale; vendor specific fns or prefer @stdlib/stats
- **density-clustering (uhho), stlnode** — dormant/niche; vendor + test or reimplement
- **danfojs** — heavy (bundles TF.js + SheetJS); prefer Arrow/DuckDB
- **regl** — intermittent; only when ECharts-GL/deck.gl don't fit
- **threads.js** — dead; use comlink
- **pdf-lib (original Hopding)** — stale (Nov 2021); use @cantoo fork
- **ElectricSQL, PowerSync, Zero, Convex** — REJECTED: server/Postgres-coupled sync engines, violate offline-only
- **bundlesize** — unmaintained; use size-limit
